newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm on short covering, off highs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm on short covering, off highs.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher but off their intraday highs on a technical bounce tied to perceptions that the market was oversold, traders said.

"This was a short-covering rally. We filled the gap between $4.26-1/2 and $4.28 (in the Dec contract). But it was a weak-kneed rally... we failed to hold on to our highs and we didn't see much follow through," a trader said.
At least two traders said volumes had been light enough Tuesday that it made it difficult to read anything into the session's price movement.
The KCBT estimated Tuesday's wheat futures volume at 34.04 million bushels, compared to 37.33 million on Monday.

KCBT wheat closed one to 11-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 3-1/4 cents at $4.28-1/2. Sept gained 11-3/4 cents to close at $4.45. Open interest in the Sept contract was reduced to 200,000 bushels at last check.

Traders said CIS was a major player, having bull-spread 3.4 million Dec/March bushels at between nine and seven cents per bushel. CIS also sold 2.6 million Dec. LG and Wolcott and Lincoln each bear-spread one million March/Dec. Dreyfus' Term Commodities bought two million March, traders said.
